title: Concrete Blocks - Crystallized Concepts for User Validation

summary.goal: Replace the 'observations-only' output of ideation with a dual-output model: Understanding (domain color) + Concrete Blocks (user-validatable mini-specs). Blocks appear in a bento-box treemap UI where size reflects concept maturity. Users validate blocks before planner handoff, solving the 'did you understand me?' problem.

problem_statement.current_state: Specialists produce freeform observations (patterns, concerns, entities). Users have no clear checkpoint to validate understanding before planning begins. They must either trust the system or read through all observations.
problem_statement.user_pain: How do I know the agents understood my idea correctly? Currently I'd need to read a PRD/spec after planning and fine-tune it.
problem_statement.gap: Specialist observations are domain-descriptive, not requirements-prescriptive. There's no intermediate artifact users can validate.

dual_output.understanding: Domain observations, concerns, patterns - the 'color' that informs HOW to plan
dual_output.blocks: Crystallized concepts (features, components, entities, flows) - the 'substance' that informs WHAT to plan

proposed_solution.user_validation_loop: Blocks appear as user discusses. User clicks to see mini-spec, approves or refines via chat. Only approved blocks go to planner.
proposed_solution.bento_box_ui: Treemap-style visualization where block size reflects concept maturity/development

acceptance_criteria.description: Specialists produce BOTH observations (understanding) AND blocks (concrete concepts)

Blocks have freeform types - common suggestions (feature, component, entity, flow, constraint, integration) but agents can use any type that fits (api_endpoint, business_rule, user_persona, edge_case, etc.)
Blocks have lifecycle: draft → reviewing → approved → revised
Each block has a mini-spec (markdown with summary, user stories, decisions, diagrams)
Blocks Panel replaces Specialists Panel in right sidebar
Blocks render as bento-box/treemap with size proportional to maturity
Clicking a block opens mini-spec detail view (modal or drawer)
User can approve block from detail view
Understanding tab shows specialist observations (existing functionality, relocated)
Planner handoff sends both understanding AND approved blocks
PlannerLead converts approved blocks into Steps

decisions.rationale: Specialists == Agents. They produce observations AND identify concrete concepts. Not two separate systems.
Visual hierarchy shows concept maturity at a glance. Larger blocks = more developed concepts.
Small, focused documents per concept. User validates incrementally, not by reading a massive spec.
Only approved blocks go to planner. User explicitly validates 'yes, this is what I meant'.
Observations are still domain-descriptive color. Blocks add the prescriptive layer on top.
Same philosophy as specialist observations - intelligence lives in agent judgment, not schema constraints. Suggested types are guidance, not limits.

observations: This is a fundamental shift from observations-only to observations+blocks
Block lifecycle (draft→approved) creates a validation checkpoint
Treemap visualization requires calculating relative weights
Planner integration changes: now receives blocks as primary input
concerns: Block extraction logic - how do agents know when a concept is 'concrete enough'?
Size calculation for treemap - what metrics drive 'maturity'?
Mini-spec format standardization across block types

observations: Bento-box treemap is unconventional but scannable
Block cards need clear type indicators (icons)
Detail view needs structured sections matching mini-spec format

current_architecture.specialists_panel: Right sidebar showing specialist cards with observations
current_architecture.understanding_tab: Tab in main area showing per-specialist observations

proposed_architecture.blocks_panel: Right sidebar showing bento-box treemap of concrete blocks

block_schema.type_notes: Suggested types: feature, component, entity, flow, constraint, integration. Agents can use ANY type that fits the concept (e.g., 'api_endpoint', 'business_rule', 'user_persona', 'edge_case'). Intelligence lives in agent judgment, not enum constraints.
block_schema.title: string
block_schema.source_context: string (which conversation turns it emerged from)

type_variations.note: These are SUGGESTIONS for common types. Agents adapt the format to fit whatever type they create.
type_variations.custom_types: Agents structure content appropriately - api_endpoint might have routes/methods, business_rule might have conditions/exceptions, etc.

bento_box_layout.max_block_size: fills available space for single high-maturity block

collapsed.icon: Type-specific icon for known types (feature=star, component=box, entity=database, flow=arrows, constraint=lock, integration=plug). Unknown/custom types get generic diamond icon.
collapsed.title: Block title (truncated if needed)
collapsed.maturity_bar: Thin bar at bottom showing maturity %

detail_view.header: Type icon + Title + Status badge + Approve button

panel_layout.empty_state: 'Concepts will emerge as you describe your idea'

notes: This is a significant evolution of ideation. The key insight: users need a validation checkpoint ('did you understand me?') BEFORE planning begins. Blocks provide focused, validatable artifacts. The bento-box visualization makes concept maturity visible at a glance.
